name: Adoption Rate

description: Relates to engineers’ uptake and sustained use of internal tools, workflows, and platforms, reflecting how effectively these resources integrate into daily workflows and solve critical problems. It serves as a key metric for assessing DevEx success and alignment with productivity goals.

name: Application Startup Duration

name: Burnout
alsoknownas: Work-life Balance Indicators
description: Evaluates developers’ mental health, job fulfillment, and workplace conditions. It serves as a critical indicator of systemic issues that harm productivity and retention.

name: Business Objective Advancement
description: Refers to measuring how effectively software development efforts align with and contribute to achieving specific organizational goals. This metric focuses on outcome-driven impact rather than raw activity metrics (e.g., lines of code, commits).

name: Change Failure Rate
description: The percentage of changes that result in degraded service or require remediation (e.g., lead to service impairment or outage, require a hotfix, rollback, fix forward, or patch).

name: CI Determinism
description: The opposite of test flakiness: the chance that a test suite’s result will be valid (not a flake) ensures that identical inputs in a continuous integration (CI) pipeline always produce the same outputs (binaries, artifacts, test results). This guarantees reproducibility, reliability, and traceability in software builds, critical for debugging, compliance, and safety-critical systems.

name: CI Pipeline Failure Rate
description: Measures the percentage of builds or automated workflows in a continuous integration (CI) system that fail due to errors (e.g., compilation issues, test failures, dependency conflicts).

name: CI Pipeline P50 Build Time
description: Refers to the median duration of successful builds in a continuous integration (CI) pipeline, representing the time by which 50% of builds complete. It is calculated by ordering all successful build durations and selecting the middle value, providing a reliable measure of typical performance while filtering out outliers.

name: Code Churn
description: Is the amount of code rewritten shortly after being written.

name: Code Review Timing and Velocity
alsoknownas: Code Review Response Times; Code Reviewer Response Time (P50 and P90); Coding vs. Code Review
description: Measures how long it takes, in business hours, for code reviewers to respond to each update of the code review from the author.

name: Code Rework Rate

name: Cognitive Load

name: Continuous Integration and Deployment (CI/CD)

name: Contribution Analysis

name: Cost Savings

This is measured by tracking how engineering improvements directly lower costs while maintaining quality and delivery speed.

name: Developer Velocity Index Benchmark
description: The Developer Velocity Index (DVI) is a survey that measures an enterprise’s technology, working practices, and organizational enablement and benchmarks them against peers. This comparison helps unearth specific areas of opportunity, whether in backlog management, testing, or security and compliance. For example, one company, well known for its technological progress and all-star developers, sought to define standard working practices more thoughtfully for cross-team collaboration after discovering a high amount of dissatisfaction, rework, and inefficiency reported by developers.

description: Aims to capture all active human developertime spent on a particular diff, split by the different roles involved. This information is made available in a privacy-aware manner. Active human work on a computer tends to be highly sequential, even if such individual sequences can be extremely short.

name: Feedback Loops

name: Flow State

name: Impact

Unlike raw outputs (e.g., lines of code), impact focuses on business results and user-centric effects of software work. Making significant contributions to one’s business unit or area of ownership, ensuring that work has a tangible impact.

name: Initiative Progress and ROI
description: Measures the financial impact and advancement of specific developer experience (DevEx) improvement projects, linking technical efforts to business outcomes. It evaluates whether investments in tools, processes, or workflows deliver measurable returns.

name: Inner / Outer Loop Time Spent
alsoknownas: Time Spent in Different Applications/Activities; Time Spent in Value-added Activities
description: To identify specific areas for improvement, it’s helpful to think of the activities involved in software development as being arranged in two loops. An inner loop comprises activities directly related to creating the product: coding, building, and unit testing. An outer loop comprises other tasks developers must do to push their code to production: integration, integration testing, releasing, and deployment. From both a productivity and personal-experience standpoint, maximizing the amount of time developers spend in the inner loop is desirable: building products directly generates value and is what most developers are excited to do. Outer-loop activities are seen by most developers as necessary but generally unsatisfying chores. Putting time into better tooling and automation for the outer loop allows developers to spend more time on inner-loop activities.

name: Interruptions
alsoknownas: Number and Nature of Interruptions
description: Measures the number of interruptions.

description:
The time it takes to go from code committed to code successfully running in production.
Measures the time between code commit and the start of the release to determine how long it takes to deliver value to your customers.

name: Line Coverage

description: Line Coverage is a code coverage metric that measures the percentage of lines in a codebase that have been executed during testing. It helps determine how well a test suite exercises the code.

name: Linting Duration

name: Mean Time to Recover

description:
Mean Time to Recover (MTTR) is a key DevOps and IT reliability metric that measures the average time it takes to restore a system after a failure. It reflects how quickly teams can diagnose, fix, and recover from incidents.
Time from bug report to fix deployment. Shows quality response capability.

name: Onboarding Time for New Members

name: Operational Activity
description: Refers to the routine tasks and processes required to maintain, monitor, and support software systems in production. These activities ensure the system remains stable, secure, and performant while minimizing downtime.

name: Operational Efficiency
description: Measures how effectively a software team or system uses resources. It focuses on optimizing workflows, reducing bottlenecks, and improving performance.

name: Operational Excellence
description: The ability of a software development team to consistently deliver high-quality software, maintain system reliability, and optimize processes while continuously improving efficiency.

name: Perceived Ability to Stay in Flow

name: Perceived Productivity
alsoknownas: Self-reported Productivity
description: The perceived productivity by an individual.

name: Perceived Rate of Delivery
description: A subjective metric that reflects how fast stakeholders (e.g., customers, executives, or internal teams) believe software is being delivered, regardless of the actual speed. It’s influenced by communication, transparency, and user experience rather than just raw deployment frequency.

name: Perceived Software Quality
description: Evaluates how users perceive the overall quality of a software product. This metric is subjective and focuses on user satisfaction, usability, and the software’s ability to meet user expectations. It often involves collecting feedback through surveys, such as Customer Satisfaction (CSAT) scores, which measure user perceptions of quality based on their experience with the product.

name: Percentage of PRs under 250 lines
description: The percentage of PRs under 250 lines. A higher percentage indicates that most PRs are relatively small, which is generally considered beneficial because smaller PRs are easier to review, less likely to introduce defects, and can be merged more quickly.

name: Percentage of Regrettable Attrition
description: Refers to the voluntary departure of highly valued employees whose loss significantly impacts the organization.

name: Percentage of Time Spent on New Capabilities
alsoknownas: Innovation rate

name: Performance
description: Relates to system efficiency, code quality, and workflow reliability, ensuring tools and processes enable developers to deliver high-quality code with minimal friction. It emphasizes both technical outcomes (e.g., system stability) and developer-centric metrics (e.g., deploy speed).

name: Post-Commit CI Speed
description: Measures how long it takes, in minutes, for each commit to get through the continuous integration (CI) pipeline.

name: Pull Request Cycle Time
description: Measures the total time a pull request spends in all stages of the development pipeline, from the first commit to when the pull request is merged into the codebase. It provides insights into the efficiency of the code review and merging process, helping teams identify bottlenecks and improve workflows.

name: Pull Request Maturity
alsoknownas: Edit Ratio; Total Number of Changelists
description: It measures the percentage of code changes that occur within a pull request after it has been submitted for review. It aims at minimizing the back-and-forth in pull requests to ensure quick and decisive reviews, leading to faster integration of code changes.

name: Pull Request Size

This includes quantiative metrics (logs for task durations, deployment statistics, and CI/CD pipeline metrics) and qualitative metrics (developer surveys, diary studies, and interviews to understand perceptions and identify pain points).
